chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: The Savoy week and what it paid (second version)
summary: A week at the Savoy, uncertain competing bands, and the low pay of fifty dollars a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah, we will make another one. The weather will be nicer too. Let's see, when you played the Savoy, how long were you at the Savoy, just a week?
We were at the Savoy a week; right.
Did you play the Lafayette Theatre also?
No, we didn't play there.
Just the Savoy.
Just the Savoy.
Who were you playing against; was it Chick's band, was Chick's band in
You know, I don't--
Fess Williams maybe?
I don't remember. It wasn't Fess, because--
Fess was in Chicago.
He was in Chicago.
He was at the Regal Theatre.

That's right. It wasn't Fess because we had seen Fess in Chicago when we were there on vacation, but we didn't play Chicago, but Fess was still in Chicago when we played there, but it wasn't against Fess. I don't remember who it was.
It could have been a lot of different bands.
I do know that every time he sees me, even today, he talks about that band.
Yeah, he's love to have that band in there on a regular basis, but they
They didn't pay no money, a hundred.
Fifty bucks a week I think was the highest they paid.
I don't remember what it was, but according--
Probably got good money compared to what the other bands were getting, but they didn't pay regular bands what it should.
I don't--
Tommy Bedford always said that he might open the Savoy, but he wouldn't stay, because they weren't paying any money.
